A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciReas, SciReas-Pro, and KRUX study. All 32 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support comparison; moved and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original frontier-model evaluations, controlled Qwen/Llama fine-tuning experiments, KRUX knowledge-probing results, and appendix validation analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds selector validation, another extractor comparison, and an experiment mixing knowledge from different questions.

M1.justification: The KRUX extraction/injection pipeline, controlled CoT SFT recipe, and default SciReas-Pro construction remain unchanged. The alternative selector and extractor configurations reuse the existing procedures for validation.

E1.justification: V3 adds a MMLU-Pro* scenario mixing matched KIs with knowledge from five other same-subject questions. The ten source benchmarks, STEM domains, and training datasets remain unchanged; SciReas-Pro-Qwen changes selection within the existing evaluation pool.

E2.justification: V3 adds Gemini-3-Pro to the frontier comparison in Figure 3, corresponding to v2 Figure 2. It also adds Gemini-3-Flash to the GPQA extractor comparison in Table 12, corresponding to v2 Table 11. Existing SFT/RL comparison models are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols select 3,208 SciReas instances using Qwen3-32B thinking on/off and mix matched KIs with randomly permuted KIs from five other same-subject questions. The reported manual KI audit changes from 100 to 300 reasoning traces. Existing training budgets, decoding settings, metrics, and original benchmark samples remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 expands validation of both benchmark construction and KRUX: Appendix B.3.2 tests dependence on proprietary selectors, while Appendix E.3 tests robustness to additional same-subject knowledge. It also extends the existing extractor analysis with Gemini-3-Flash and a larger manual audit. These additions address distinct validity questions beyond the earlier checks.

E5.justification: Both versions retain means and standard deviations over five KI permutations, 30 samples for sampling validation, and the existing confidence-interval reporting. V3 introduces no new repeated-run, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation practice; the larger manual audit concerns sample size.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged. V3 adds Gemini-3-Pro frontier points, Gemini-3-Flash extraction results, and new Tables 8 and 14. For example, o3 scores 73.4/77.8 under low/high effort on SciReas-Pro-Qwen, and Qwen scores 64.9 with mixed KIs on MMLU-Pro*. These are newly reported conditions, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The standard SFT objective and input/reasoning-trace/answer formalization in v2 Appendix E.1 are retained in v3 Appendix D.1. No substantive mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and three central findings: knowledge retrieval is a bottleneck, reasoning models benefit from external KIs, and CoT helps surface existing knowledge. The new validation evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V3 removes v2 Appendix A's substantive limitations concerning small-model generalizability, contamination, incomplete STEM coverage, and KI reliability. It adds interpretations that the Qwen selector supports selector independence and mixed-KI gains support generalizable knowledge. Some main-text caveats about distinguishing missing knowledge from retrieval difficulties remain.

D1.justification: V3 documents reproducible construction details for the new checks, including the Qwen3-32B thinking toggle and mixing KIs from five same-subject questions before permutation. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, prompt templates, and code/artifact access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A limited set of cited sources changes, including replacement of the introductory Zhao et al. (2023) scientific-research survey citation with Luo et al. (2025). The main positioning against existing benchmarks and knowledge/reasoning probes remains stable. Most other bibliography edits update metadata or remove duplicate entries.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, promotes the research questions to Sections 4.3–4.5, adds an Impact Statement, and removes the Limitations section. Affiliations and publication information are updated. Most narrative content and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: The frontier plot and reasoning-intensity example are resized, reordered, and placed side by side; the example now omits the question text, and the plot changes its legend and axis presentation. V3 adds Tables 8 and 14 and expands the GPQA extractor table. Other displays mainly retain their designs while moving or being renumbered.

improvement.justification: The open-selector validation and expanded extractor checks strengthen empirical support. However, v3 removes material limitations about model-size generalization, contamination, and KI reliability. Its new mixed-KI test retains matched KIs, so it does not isolate answer leakage or solution hints as strongly as its interpretation suggests. The added validation and loss of qualification leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
